title: Most common word
instructorPromptText: Write a C function `void find_most_common_word(const char *text, char *result)` that finds the word that appears most frequently in a string of space-separated words, and copies it into the result buffer. Assume words are case-insensitive and ignore punctuation.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program correctly parse and separate the text into individual words using loops or `strtok`?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Tokenizing character buffers in C requires careful pointer management since C has no built-in string splitting methods.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program avoid modifying the input string directly (which is `const char*` and may reside in read-only memory)?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Modifying a string literal in C (e.g., using `strtok` on the original input without making a copy) results in a segmentation fault.

specGateDimensions.description: How does the program count unique word occurrences? Does it declare a structure array or parallel arrays to store words and their counts?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Without high-level dictionaries, C students must manage parallel arrays or struct arrays (e.g. struct { char word[50]; int count; }) to count frequencies.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student attempts to mutate the read-only input string directly, causing a segmentation fault.
Student does not copy the extracted word into a local writable buffer before tokenizing.
Student defines a `WordCount` struct to group each word with its integer frequency count, representing robust code architecture.
Student goes out of bounds on the structure array because they do not track the number of unique words found.
Student compares words case-sensitively, counting 'The' and 'the' as separate words.
